kicker: Two days on designing public services that people can actually use: forms, letters, queues, procurement and the people who sign them off.

venue.name: Albion Mill
rows: Albion Mill, 14 Canal Wharf, Leeds LS1 4BR
9 minutes on foot, flat, along the canal towpath
Every room. A lift to the Loft and the Workroom
Induction loop in the Hall. Live captions on every Hall session
Sessions marked BSL in the programme, and others on request until 4 March
Room D on the ground floor, open 08:30 to 18:30

people.name: Nadia Okonkwo-Hale
people.role: Head of design, a northern city council
people.says: If a resident has to phone us to finish a form, the form has failed, however good it looks.

people.name: Tomasz Wierzbicki
people.role: Content lead, a national benefits agency
people.says: We read 40,000 letters. The median one needed a reading age of 16. We got it to 11 without losing a single legal clause.

people.name: Ama Boateng
people.role: Service owner, a regional transport authority
people.says: The ticket office queue is a service too. We redesigned the floor tape before we touched the app.

people.name: Priya Raman
people.says: A £20 voucher for a ninety-minute interview is not a thank you. Here is the rate card we use and why.

people.name: Ruth Calloway
people.says: An audit that ends in a PDF changes nothing. One that ends in a budget line changes the next five years.

people.name: Felix Achterberg
people.says: The contract decides what the team is allowed to learn. Write the learning into the contract.
